title: Many Nichiren communities
hook: Nichiren Shu, Nichiren Shoshu, Soka Gakkai and others differ in important ways; each speaks for itself

segments.voice: Yesterday, the gohonzon: the written mandala, the title down its center and a whole assembly around it. Your line: the scroll.

Ask a handful of Nichiren Buddhists who Nichiren was, which scroll matters most and who keeps the teaching, and the answers won't all match. Each will be sincere. Each will come with reasons, and a history of its own. A fair listener's first job is a plain one: let each answer finish before reaching for a verdict. That's today, and it closes a week among Japan's temple schools, from Tendai's mountain to Shingon's mandalas to the chanted title.
screen: `THE ANSWERS DON'T ALL MATCH.` → `LET EACH ONE FINISH.` → `A WEEK IN JAPAN'S SCHOOLS.`

segments.voice: Here are three, each as it describes itself, none ranked. First, Nichiren Shu. It sees itself as carrying on the temple lineages of Nichiren's disciples. It honors Nichiren as a great teacher and bodhisattva sent to spread the Lotus Sutra, and places Shakyamuni, the eternal Buddha of the Lotus Sutra, at the center of devotion. Its temples may hold statues as well as scrolls, and its members often chant namu myoho renge kyo. Second, Nichiren Shoshu. It traces its line through Nikko, one of Nichiren's senior disciples, to a head temple at the foot of Mount Fuji, Taiseki-ji. It teaches that Nichiren himself is the true Buddha for this age, and reveres one great scroll kept at the head temple as the heart of its faith. Its priests confer the gohonzon on members. Third, Soka Gakkai. It began in Japan as a society of lay educators connected to Nichiren Shoshu. The two later parted ways, and the separation still matters to both. Soka Gakkai now describes itself as a lay Buddhist movement, with members far beyond Japan, built on chanting, study and small discussion meetings in members' homes, and on work for peace, culture and education. And there are others: Rissho Kosei-kai, Reiyukai, and the monks of Nipponzan Myohoji, who walk beating drums and build peace pagodas. Each is a sangha, and each claims to be faithful to Nichiren. They differ on who he was, which scroll is true, and whether priests or laypeople carry the teaching. Those aren't small questions, which is exactly why each deserves to be heard in its own voice, not through a rival's summary, and not through mine.
screen: `NICHIREN SHU: THE TEMPLE LINEAGES.` · `NICHIREN SHOSHU: THE HEAD TEMPLE.` · `SOKA GAKKAI: A LAY MOVEMENT.` · `OTHERS, EACH IN ITS OWN WORDS.` · then, large: `EACH SPEAKS FOR ITSELF.`

segments.voice: Choose one community from today, recall one thing it says about itself in its own words, and hold that sentence for a few breaths without adding a but. Then think of a group you belong to, a family, a team, a faith, a town, and the first sentence you'd want a stranger to hear about it. Sit with the two sentences side by side.
Many Nichiren communities. Nichiren Shu, Nichiren Shoshu, Soka Gakkai and others: one chant, one sutra, and real differences, each explained in its own voice. Today's word.
Your line: each speaks for itself. A fair hearing comes before any verdict. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Nichiren Buddhists belong to several communities, among them Nichiren Shu, Nichiren Shoshu and Soka Gakkai, which share the Lotus Sutra and the chanted title but differ on Nichiren's role, the gohonzon and the place of priests and laypeople.

chat.says: Aren't all the Nichiren groups basically one church with different names?
options: No. They share the chant, but differ on who Nichiren was and which scroll is true.
Yes. They split only over which language to chant in, and agree on everything else.
Yes. They're all run from one head temple at the foot of Mount Fuji.

notes: Please have each community's description checked against its own materials (Nichiren Shu, Nichiren Shoshu, Soka Gakkai); the script aims to state each view without ranking.
Nichiren Shu: 'great teacher and bodhisattva' (often identified with Bodhisattva Superior Practices / Jogyo) and Shakyamuni as the eternal Buddha at the center: confirm.
Nichiren Shoshu: Nikko lineage, Taiseki-ji, Nichiren as True Buddha, the Dai-Gohonzon, priests conferring gohonzon: confirm.

Soka Gakkai: origin among lay educators (Makiguchi, Toda) linked to Nichiren Shoshu, later separation (deliberately undated), now issuing its own gohonzon (not stated in voice): confirm the neutral phrasing 'parted ways'.
Rissho Kosei-kai, Reiyukai, Nipponzan Myohoji listed as 'others'; confirm all three identify with the Nichiren / Lotus Sutra stream.
